title: Sewn clothing and the eyed needle
summary: People wore prepared hides long before needles, and bone awls let them sew fitted garments. The earliest known eyed needles appear about 40,000 years ago at Denisova Cave in Siberia, by 38,000 in the Caucasus, 30,000 in East Asia and 26,000 in Europe; the excavators called one Denisova needle 50,000 years old. Eyed needles made sewing finer and quicker, suiting layered clothing against glacial cold, and as personal ornaments came to be sewn onto clothes, dress took on social meaning beyond warmth.

uncertainty.note: Denisova needle dated in initial reports to c. 50,000 years ago; broader Eurasian chronology by Gilligan et al. (2024) places early eyed needles from ~40,000 cal BP.

as_recorded.value: beginning from ~40,000 cal B.P. at Denisova Cave

where.modern_name: Denisova Cave, Altai Krai, Siberia, Russia (reference site for the earliest Siberian eyed needle; eyed bone needles also appear across Upper Paleolithic Eurasia)
where.historical_name: Denisova Cave in the Altai Mountains, southern Siberia; no polities or formal place names exist at this date

importance.justification: Fine sewing made layered, fitted clothing practical and helped humans live through glacial cold (R3 D3 T4 L2).

sources.title: Paleolithic eyed needles and the evolution of dress (Science Advances 10:eadp2887)
sources.author: Ian Gilligan, Francesco d'Errico, Luc Doyon, Wei Wang, Yaroslav V. Kuzmin
